article_title: Evidence for the Frontline: Evaluation Report and Executive Summary
citation: Lord, P., Sims, D., White, R., & Roy, P. (2017). Evidence for the Frontline: Evaluation report and executive summary. Education Endowment Foundation. http://www.evidenceforthefrontline.com/
title: Evidence for the Frontline (E4F) online evidence brokerage service
description: E4F is "an online brokerage service designed to provide teachers and school leaders with timely access to relevant evidence on supporting young people's learning". Teachers post their own questions about improving teaching and learning on a bespoke web-based interface; a broker matches each question to an academic researcher, signposts published evidence or existing answers, or helps the user frame the question. It was developed by Sandringham School and the Institute for Effective Education at the University of York with the Coalition for Evidence Based Education, and piloted in 32 schools in 2015/16.
requirements: A broker mediates between teachers and recruited research academics, matching questions to relevant evidence experts or existing resources
Each participating school nominates a school champion to promote the service and act as point of contact
constraints: Full summaries for practical application (one-page templates) were judged beyond the scope and budget of the pilot and were not actioned
target_learners: Teachers and school leaders in primary, secondary and special schools
target_learning_goals: Effective engagement with and use of research evidence to improve teaching and pupils' learning
examples: Example questions posted included whether studies explore the influence of inter-school collaboration on student outcomes, and whether pupils perform better when their Science teacher teaches within their specialism up to Key Stage 4
key_sources: Lord, P., Sims, D., White, R., & Roy, P. (2017). Evidence for the Frontline: Evaluation report and executive summary. Education Endowment Foundation. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED581162

article_title: Evidence for the Frontline: Evaluation Report and Executive Summary
citation: Lord, P., Sims, D., White, R., & Roy, P. (2017). Evidence for the Frontline: Evaluation report and executive summary. Education Endowment Foundation. http://www.evidenceforthefrontline.com/
title: Linkage and dialogue as two key elements of effective knowledge transfer between research and the classroom
description: The E4F service was conceived around two elements the literature identifies as effective in knowledge transfer between research and the classroom: "(1) linkage between knowledge or evidence and practice, and (2) dialogue and interaction between teachers and researchers". Linkage is where evidence is translated for use in practice, usually mediated via intermediaries, with the brokerage function conceived as part of that linkage process to help ensure questions were framed appropriately and matched to relevant academics. The report notes social interaction is a key element of effective knowledge transfer, while effective linkage or brokerage is one of the least well researched areas.
requirements: Intermediaries (brokers) who translate and match evidence to practice questions
Social interaction and dialogue between teachers and researchers
constraints: The report states effective linkage or brokerage is one of the least well researched areas of knowledge transfer, citing Becheikh et al. (2009) and Nelson and O'Beirne (2014)
target_learners: Teachers and school leaders engaging with research evidence
target_learning_goals: Schools' engagement with and use of research evidence in teaching and learning
examples: The E4F brokerage service operationalised both elements: brokers supported question framing and matching (linkage), and the service connected teachers directly with research academics (dialogue)
key_sources: Lord, P., Sims, D., White, R., & Roy, P. (2017). Evidence for the Frontline: Evaluation report and executive summary. Education Endowment Foundation. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED581162
